elements.element: Customer may terminate for convenience during the term.
elements.evidence: The added sentence expressly provides: “The Company may terminate this Agreement for convenience at any time.”

elements.element: Customer termination for convenience requires 30 days' notice.
elements.evidence: The clause requires ninety (90) days' notice, not 30 days' notice.

elements.element: Customer's termination notice must be written.
elements.evidence: The added convenience-termination right requires “ninety (90) days written notice.”

elements.element: Customer is entitled to a refund of prepaid fees upon termination for convenience.
elements.evidence: No operative language requires HDI to refund prepaid fees. The payment provision does not demonstrably establish that prepaid fees cannot exist.

elements.element: Any refund of prepaid fees must be calculated pro rata.
elements.evidence: The redlined clause contains no pro-rata refund obligation or calculation.

elements.element: Vendor has no right to terminate for convenience during a committed term.
elements.evidence: Any Termination Date specified by HDI must be “the end of the then-current term,” so HDI cannot terminate effective during the committed term.
The clause expressly states that the Company “may terminate this Agreement for convenience at any time.”

elements.element: Customer termination for convenience requires between 60 and 90 days' notice.
elements.evidence: The clause requires ninety (90) days' written notice, which is within the permitted 60–90 day range.

elements.element: Any early-termination fee payable by Customer must not exceed three months' fees.
elements.evidence: The Termination Payment is capped at “the amounts payable by the Company under Section 3.1 for the three (3) months preceding the Termination Date.”

elements.element: Vendor may terminate for convenience only effective at the end of a term.
elements.evidence: The proviso requires any Termination Date specified by HDI to be “the end of the then-current term.”

elements.element: Vendor termination for convenience requires 90 days' notice.
elements.evidence: The general termination right remains subject to “ninety (90) days written notice to the other,” including termination by HDI.

result.reason: The redline fully reaches the fallback: Company receives an express convenience-termination right on 90 days' written notice, its Termination Payment is capped at three months' Section 3.1 fees, and HDI may terminate only at term-end on 90 days' notice. It does not reach the preferred position because Company does not receive a 30-day notice period or any pro-rata refund of prepaid fees. The changes are confined to the targeted termination rights and fee cap, although the express Company termination sentence is somewhat duplicative of the existing general termination language.
